intro: Exam-style performance-based tasks for A+ Core 1: mobile devices, RAID, small-office networking, hardware repair and troubleshooting.

questions.title: Set up a corporate phone
questions.scenario: A new employee receives a company-owned smartphone. Walk through setup in a sensible order, then match printer symptoms to causes for a second ticket.

activities.title: Order the setup steps
activities.prompt: Put the steps in a logical order.
items: Power on and connect to Wi-Fi
Sign in to the manufacturer account (Apple ID or Google)
Enroll the device in the company MDM
Install the email profile and configure the Exchange account
Set a PIN or biometric lock
Send and receive a test email

activities.title: Printer symptoms
activities.prompt: Drag each symptom to the part or setting most likely at fault.

items.text: Toner smears when you touch the page
Several sheets are pulled at once or the tray will not feed
Repeating marks or vertical streaks on every page
Printer is powered on but shows as offline

questions.explanation: Enroll in MDM before loading corporate data so policies (encryption, lock, remote wipe) apply from the start. Smearing toner means the fuser is not melting it onto the page; feeding problems point at the pickup roller; repeating marks come from the drum; an offline printer is usually network, port or driver.

questions.title: RAID capacity and levels
questions.scenario: A client wants to know how much usable space each array gives. All disks are 2 TB unless stated.

activities.title: Match the description to the RAID level
activities.prompt: Drag each description to the level.

items.text: Striping only, no fault tolerance
Mirror of two disks
Striping with single parity, three disks minimum
Double parity, survives two failed disks
Mirrored pairs that are striped, four disks minimum

questions.explanation: Usable capacity: RAID 0 = n x size, RAID 1 = one disk, RAID 5 = (n-1) x size, RAID 6 = (n-2) x size, RAID 10 = n/2 x size. RAID 5 survives one failed disk, RAID 6 two, RAID 10 one per mirror pair.

questions.title: Secure a small-office router
questions.scenario: A new SOHO router arrives with factory settings. Sort the actions into those you should do and those you must avoid.

activities.title: Do or don't
activities.prompt: Drag each action to the right group.

items.text: Change the default administrator password
Use WPA3 or WPA2 with AES
Disable WPS
Keep the firmware updated
Leave remote administration open to the internet
Use WEP so older devices still connect
Keep the default admin username and password
Broadcast the admin page on the guest network

activities.title: Identify the setting
activities.prompt: Name the router feature that fits each need.

rows.label: Give a printer the same IP every time without setting it on the printer
Expose an internal web server to the internet on a chosen port
Separate visitor Wi-Fi from the company network

questions.explanation: Harden defaults: change credentials, use WPA3/WPA2-AES, disable WPS and remote administration, update firmware. DHCP reservations bind an address to a MAC; port forwarding publishes an internal service; a guest network isolates visitors.

questions.title: Replace laptop memory
questions.scenario: A laptop needs more RAM. Put the safe procedure in order, then pick the likely failing component for three symptoms.

activities.title: Order the procedure
items: Power off, unplug the charger and remove the battery if possible
Put on an ESD strap and work on a clean, non-static surface
Release the clips and remove the old module
Insert the new module at an angle and press it down until the clips lock
Close the panel, reconnect power and confirm the new size in the BIOS or OS

activities.title: Match the symptom to the part
activities.prompt: Drag each symptom to the most likely component.

items.text: No lights or fans at all
Continuous beeps and no display after a memory change
Clicking noise, then 'operating system not found'
Random shutdowns under load with loud fans

questions.explanation: Always power down, remove power and use ESD protection. RAM seats at an angle, then clicks down. Beep codes at POST with no video after a change point to RAM; clicking from the drive points at storage; overheating shutdowns point at cooling.

questions.title: Cables, tools and ports
questions.scenario: A technician's bag holds several tools and the network closet has labelled ports. Match each tool or port to its job.

activities.title: Match the tool to the job
activities.prompt: Drag each job to the tool.

items.text: Check continuity and pinout of a patch cable
Trace which wall jack a cable goes to
Attach an RJ-45 connector to a cable
Test whether a network port transmits and receives
Find the least crowded wireless channel

activities.title: Match the port to its service
activities.prompt: Drag each port number to the service.

questions.explanation: Cable testers check wiring, toner and probe trace cables, crimpers terminate RJ-45, loopback plugs test ports and Wi-Fi analyzers show channel use. Ports: HTTPS 443, RDP 3389, SSH 22, DNS 53, DHCP server 67 (client 68).

questions.title: Hardware symptoms
questions.scenario: Five desktops were reported with different problems. Match each to the most likely component, then order the troubleshooting steps.

activities.title: Match symptom to component
activities.prompt: Drag each symptom to the most likely cause.

items.text: No power, no fans, no lights
Beeps on boot and no display
Fans spin, but the monitor says 'No signal'
Shuts down after a few minutes under load
Slow, clicking, files will not open

activities.title: Order the troubleshooting steps
activities.prompt: Put the CompTIA steps in order.
items: Establish a theory of probable cause

questions.explanation: Match the symptom to the component, test your theory, and follow the standard methodology each time. A monitor reporting no signal while fans spin often means a loose cable, wrong input or failed GPU rather than a dead PC.
